items.title: Allan Jaffe Interview, 1969-04-16
items.q: Well, I knew when we looked, Dr. Orstin went back a bit.

ctx.x: Peers, Jack Peers. Yes. Our next door neighbor, when we were living here, somebody from Philadelphia. He came over one night and said, this is no way to run a business. He took the thing. Well, first of all, he was six foot six, you know. I'd stand there, you know, just not let people in. We're out. I don't remember when we went to fifty cent minimum. But the dollar, I think it was the dollar, we went to, we left three ladies here watching the whole night. June Conn and two of her girlfriends, they're all…

Well, I knew when we looked, Dr. Orstin went back a bit. It was when they took us to Function Society, we went out with working with little angels. And we came home. And we walked into the door and one of the ladies wouldn't let me in because they were going to pay a dollar. And I was going to get down the two and grabbed my horn and said, hey, you know, please put a dollar in here if you want to come inside.

Well, can we touch the subject side to the actual musical aspects of the hall and the people that you were, how you decided to go about choosing a particular band and particularly is to be used in a book about George Lewis. What sort of role do you feel that George played in the development of the hall and it's, you know, kind of working out? He was one of the, you know, few musicians whose name I knew before I came here. You know, the people, you know, involved with the punk band, you know, records I heard, of…
